summary:
The ACES Act of 2025 (Public Law 119-32, enacted August 14, 2025) directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to seek to enter into an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (National Academies) to conduct a study on the prevalence and mortality of cancers among individuals who served on active duty as aircrew on fixed-wing aircraft in the Armed Forces. The Act does not appropriate funds or amend the U.S. Code.

Section 2(a) requires the Secretary, not later than 30 days after enactment, to seek to enter into such an agreement. The Secretary must finalize the agreement not later than 60 days after entering negotiations. If the Secretary fails to meet that deadline, the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Veterans’ Affairs of the Senate and House a report explaining the failure and providing an estimated date for finalization, and shall provide briefings to those committees not less frequently than every 60 days thereafter until the agreement is finalized.

Section 2(b) specifies the study’s content. The study must: (1) identify exposures associated with military occupations of covered individuals, including chemicals, compounds, agents, and other phenomena; (2) review the literature to determine associations between those exposures and overall cancer morbidity and mortality, as well as increased incidence or prevalence of brain, colon and rectal, kidney, lung, melanoma skin, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, pancreatic, prostate, testicular, thyroid, urinary bladder, and other cancers as determined appropriate by the Secretary in consultation with the National Academies; and (3) determine, to the extent possible, the prevalence of and mortality from the specified cancers among covered individuals using available data sources, which may include Department of Veterans Affairs, Department of Defense, and individual Service health care and administrative databases, the national death index maintained by the National Center for Health Statistics, and the study conducted under section 750 of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (Public Law 116-283).

At the study’s conclusion, the National Academies shall submit a report of the results to the Secretary and the House and Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committees (Section 2(c)). Section 2(d) defines “covered individual” as a person who served on active duty in the Army, Navy, Air Force, or Marine Corps as an aircrew member of a fixed-wing aircraft, including as a pilot, navigator, weapons systems operator, aircraft system operator, or any other crew member who regularly flew in a fixed-wing aircraft. No further authorizations, appropriations, or regulatory authorities are provided.
